records.play-introduction: welcome to billiards play. your table, your friends, and twenty ways to run the rack. pick a game, enter your players, and tap the speaker to hear the calls live while you score right off the rail. check the house rules, grab a remote, and let us see who owns the cloth tonight.
records.rules-kelly: kelly pool. lowest ball on the table must be struck first. pocket a ball legally to keep shooting. your mission: secretly sink your private number to win. if an opponent pockets your ball, you get dealt a fresh live number from the pool. run out of spare numbers? re-rack and redeal. fouled pots spot back up.
records.setup-kelly: kelly pool. 2 to 8 players. standard 15-ball rack. enter your players in shooting order. check your secret numbers on your individual screens, or use the private view on the host. keep those numbers hidden, and step up to break.
records.rules-bounty: secret bounty. five fast rounds, one shot per visit. every legal ball scores one point, but sink your secret bounty ball to pocket two bonus points. bounties can overlap across players, and whenever a target drops, a fresh bounty is secretly dealt for your next turn. highest score takes the match.
records.setup-bounty: secret bounty. 2 to 6 players. standard 15-ball rack. check your opening secret target on your device, set your shooting order, and start hunting points.
records.rules-saboteur: undercover saboteur. four tense rounds of pure shotmaking and paranoia. one player is secretly sabotaging the runout. the crew's objective: make enough legal scoring shots to reach double the player count. the saboteur wins if the crew falls short. after round two, cast a private vote on who is throwing shots. nail the traitor by strict majority for a one-point crew bonus at the reveal. each legal scoring shot adds one, even when several balls drop. you may abstain from the vote. roles stay hidden until the final reveal.
records.setup-saboteur: undercover saboteur. 4 to 8 players. full 15-ball rack. keep screens shielded—one of you is playing for the other side.
records.rules-highlow: high-low. one table, two opposing missions. one player must strike the lowest ball on the felt; the other must hit the highest. pocket any legal ball to score a point and keep the turn. first shooter to eight points takes the frame. swap high-low roles and alternate breaks each rack. best two of three racks wins. foul pots spot back up.
records.setup-highlow: high-low. 2 players. standard 15-ball rack. player one opens on low; player two opens on high, break them open, and race to eight.
records.rules-ghost: ghost runout. you versus the table. break the rack, take ball in hand anywhere, and run the table in strict rotation. break pots count and break scratches are forgiven. once you place the cue ball, zero mistakes allowed: the first miss or foul hands the rack to the ghost. clear the table to earn the point. race to five racks. the highest ball spots back up if pocketed before the others are cleared. clear the entire rack on the break, and you win that rack.
records.setup-ghost: ghost runout. solo match. choose your ball count (3, 6, 9, or 10-ball) to dial in your target difficulty. rack tight and take the break.
records.rules-cutthroat: cutthroat. three-player survival pool. claim your group: 1–5, 6–10, or 11–15. your goal is to run your opponents' balls off the table while protecting your own. keep shooting as long as you legally pocket any ball. scratch, and all pocketed balls stay down, but one ball spots up for every opponent—bringing eliminated players straight back into the fight. last survivor wins. losing your last ball ends your turn. other foul pots spot back up. if every group is cleared together, spot one ball per group and keep playing.
records.setup-cutthroat: cutthroat. 3 players. standard 15-ball triangle. claim your five numbers, set your shooting order, and protect your set.
records.rules-killer: killer. pure pressure. every shooter starts with three lives and gets exactly one shot per turn. sink a ball to stay safe; miss or commit a foul to lose a life. a scratch on the break burns an instant life; a dry break gets one retry. re-rack whenever the table empties. last player standing wins. only a legal dry break earns the free retry.
records.setup-killer: killer. 2 to 12 players. standard 15-ball rack. lock in the shooting order, watch the life counter, and do not leave an easy hanger.
records.rules-horse: h-o-r-s-e. call-shot execution at its best. the leader picks a shot from the bank and shoots. miss, and leadership passes clean. make it, and every remaining player must pull off that exact same shot. miss the replica, take a letter. five letters eliminates you. last survivor claims the table. reset the identical layout for each attempt. after the challenge, leadership moves to the next surviving player.
records.setup-horse: h-o-r-s-e. 2 to 6 players. pick your rotation order, let player one choose the opening layout, and call the line.
records.rules-speed: speed pool. run the rack against the stopwatch. the clock starts on break contact and stops the instant your final ball drops. every foul adds a brutal 10-second penalty and spots the pocketed balls. each player gets two full attempts—fastest valid time takes the crown. penalties count toward your time. pausing or leaving a running attempt marks it interrupted, so it cannot win.
records.setup-speed: speed pool. 1 to 6 players. standard rack. have your table-side spotter ready on the controls, chalk up, and start the clock as you break.
records.rules-three: three-ball. fast, short, and unforgiving. three balls, three rounds. every stroke counts as one point, starting with the break. fouls cost an extra penalty stroke and spot the balls. clear the rack in as few strokes as possible, capped at six strokes per attempt. lowest cumulative score after three rounds wins.
records.setup-three: three-ball. 1 to 8 players. rack a tight three-ball triangle. break with control, play position, and keep the stroke count low.
records.rules-poker: poker pool. turn your shotmaking into a winning five-card hand. five rounds, one shot per visit. make a legal pot and privately draft the best of two cards. miss or foul, and you receive a single random card. after five rounds, the best poker hand takes the table. several pots on one shot still earn just one card choice. equal hands tie; suits never break the tie. re-rack when empty. a legal break needs a pot or four object balls to cushions; one dry illegal-break retry is free.
records.setup-poker: poker pool. 2 to 6 players. standard 15-ball rack. enter your card sharks and keep devices private between visits.
records.rules-blackjack: twenty-one (blackjack). hit or stand right on the felt across three hands. start with two hidden cards. stand whenever your total looks solid, or take a shot to hit: pocket a ball to draw a card, miss and your turn stands, foul and you bust out. aces count 1 or 11, face cards are 10, and hitting 21 stands automatically. closest to 21 without busting takes the point. tied hands each earn a point. most hand points after three hands wins.
records.setup-blackjack: twenty-one (blackjack). 2 to 6 players. standard 15-ball rack. check your opening deal, calculate the odds, and step into the shot.
records.rules-cribbage: cribbage pool. precision pairing. pocket balls that add up to 15: 1 and 14, 2 and 13, on through 7 and 8. the moment you pocket an unpaired ball, you are on the hook—sink at least one matching partner on your very next stroke, or all held balls spot back up and your turn ends. the 15-ball scores as the final bonus point once all pairs are cleared. first to five points wins. a foul returns held balls and foul pots. completed pairs stay scored. an early fifteen spots back up. a final four-all score is a draw.
records.setup-cribbage: cribbage pool. 2 players. standard 15-ball rack. map your pairs, control the cue ball, and do not get trapped holding an open partner.
records.rules-bingo: billiards bingo. nine shot challenges laid out across each player’s custom grid. choose an open square, set the shot layout, and fire away. make it to stamp the card. complete any row, column, or diagonal line to claim a win at the end of the full round. joint winners are possible. if nobody hits a line after ten rounds, most completed squares takes it. bank and kick shots must follow the named route. draw and follow shots must finish in the shown zone.
records.setup-bingo: billiards bingo. 2 to 6 players. check your individual bingo board, pick your route, and take on square one.
records.rules-ring: ring game. five nine-ball racks of escalating action. shoot in strict numerical rotation. pocketing a legal ball keeps your turn alive. the 5-ball scores one point; the 9-ball scores two points when pocketed as the final ball. fouls award the next player ball in hand. rotate the break every rack—most points at the end takes the prize. an early nine spots back up, and foul pots return to the table.
records.setup-ring: ring game. 3 to 6 players. standard 9-ball diamond. set your shooting order and target the money balls.
records.rules-turf: turf war. eight rounds of table control. sinking a legal ball captures that specific pocket for you. at the end of every round, you score one point for every pocket you hold. pocketing balls in enemy pockets flips the territory to you. fouls award zero turf. most points after eight rounds wins. pocket ownership survives a re-rack.
records.setup-turf: turf war. 2 to 4 players. standard 15-ball rack. set your rotation and battle to lock down the corner pockets.
records.rules-battleship: battleship billiards. tactical naval warfare on green felt. each player secretly locks a 3-cell cruiser and a 2-cell destroyer on a 3×3 grid. a legal scoring shot earns one missile strike on an enemy grid coordinate, even when several balls drop. miss or foul, and your turn passes without an attack. first captain to sink all five enemy coordinates wins. attack only untried coordinates. re-racks preserve the fleets.
records.setup-battleship: battleship billiards. 2 players. full rack. lock in your hidden ship coordinates on your screens before taking the break.
records.rules-golf: golf pool. six holes, six designated cups: top-left, top-middle, top-right, bottom-right, bottom-middle, and bottom-left. place the cue ball on the head spot and the object ball on the center spot. knock it straight into the target pocket. every stroke counts. wrong pockets add one stroke; scratches cost two. ten-stroke cap per hole. lowest six-hole score wins. other fouls add one stroke; only the largest penalty applies on a shot. reset after a wrong pocket or foul.
records.setup-golf: golf pool. 1 to 6 players. place the object ball on center, cue ball on the head spot, and tee off on hole 1.
records.rules-bowliards: bowliards. ten frames of pool-bowling scoring. each frame gives you two innings to clear a fresh 10-ball rack. the break is free—all pocketed break balls spot up with no score or penalty. clear all ten balls on visit one for a strike; clean up the rest on visit two for a spare. standard bowling bonuses apply. highest pinfall takes the match. an inning continues while you pot; a miss or foul ends it. foul pots spot back up. in frame ten, a strike earns two bonus innings and a spare earns one. re-rack whenever a bonus inning starts with an empty table.
records.setup-bowliards: bowliards. 1 to 4 players. rack a tight 10-ball triangle for each frame. break clean, run the pins, and hunt for strikes.
records.rules-equalizer: equalizer. the level-playing-field test. five challenging three-ball layouts where both players shoot the identical setup. players receive an allowance of 0, 1, or 2 permitted misses, plus one cue-ball reposition per layout. clear all three balls within your miss limit to bank a point; fouls end the run immediately. most cleared layouts wins.
records.setup-equalizer: equalizer. 2 players. assign each shooter's miss allowance based on skill level, set up layout 1, and alternate opening attempts.
records.house-rules: fouls trump pots every time. scratch or foul, and pocketed balls spot back up while incoming gets ball in hand anywhere on the table—unless game rules say otherwise. call it honest, shoot it clean, and use undo if someone fat-fingers the tally.
records.table-tools: level up your table. sync a bluetooth remote for hands-free scoring, dial in custom shot clocks with automated warnings, or launch drill mode to track shooting percentages. when you are ready to calibrate table ballistics, measure cloth speed and cushion bounce with guided measurements. use back to table at the top or bottom to return to the game choices, or tap outside this window to go back to where you were.
records.clicker-help: keep your hands on your cue. pair your bluetooth clicker in device settings and map buttons for single-click scoring. using a supported offline voice app? call the table directly: table, made; table, miss; table, foul; table, scratch; or table, undo. turn referee audio on to hear the calls announced out loud. in games that track ball numbers, say table, ball one made, or use the number of the ball you pocketed.
records.clock-help: put real match pressure on every shot. the host runs the timer with custom shot lengths and player extensions. each recorded shot resets the timer, and time is announced when time expires. step up and beat the clock. expiry does not automatically record a foul.
records.drill-help: track your stroke and build consistency. choose your attempts, set your rep targets, and log makes versus misses. the app tracks your conversion rate live and rotates shooters after each completed set.
records.host-seat-help: claim your seat at the table. reserving your seat keeps your player view and host controls together. a phone assigned to that same seat returns to waiting. keep your screen angled away when viewing private roles or targets.
records.private-view-help: shield your screen before opening this view. secret cards, bounty targets, saboteur roles, and naval coordinates never play over table audio to keep your secrets safe.
records.foul-help: if the game tracks ball numbers, tap the made balls first, then select scratch or foul. the table resolves balls and penalties in a single step. tap undo if you need to correct a call.
records.local-table-help: host a local room right over your private wi-fi—no outside internet needed. fire up the host in the supported windows app or android play preview, show the qr code, and let players scan in from their phones. once you approve their seat, their private screens sync instantly. keep every device on the same private wi-fi, and keep the host running.
records.clear-game-help: reset the table. clearing your game wipes the current match log and disconnects connected players so you can pick a fresh game mode. drills, remotes, and table calibration settings stay saved.
records.calibration-overview: measure the real physics of your cloth and cushions. set up a level table, clean balls, and film side-on at 60 frames per second with a measuring tape in frame. repeat at least three times in both directions and on different cushions. these measurements estimate rolling resistance and effective cushion response; they do not measure sliding friction or spin transfer.
records.calibration-cloth: roll a clean ball smoothly with zero side spin. track distance in meters and time in seconds from where the ball begins rolling pure until it comes to a dead stop. enter your numbers to estimate your table’s rolling resistance. keep clear of every cushion. count video frames for timing, rather than using a hand stopwatch.
records.calibration-cushion: send a ball squarely into the rail at 90 degrees with no spin. from your video frames, measure the distance traveled over equal time windows right before contact and after the rebound. enter incoming and outgoing distances to calculate your cushion’s effective rebound setting. avoid the impact frame, cushion compression, and the first few frames of sliding after rebound. repeat at several gentle speeds.
